about: Curated KJV English glosses (not a full historic dictionary). g=meaning, s=how to read, w=why it matters today, x=sample refs.

charity.g: Often means self-giving love (caritas), not fundraising or a donation drive.
charity.s: In 1 Corinthians 13, read “charity” as steadfast love.
charity.w: When kindness feels out of reach, “charity” in the KJV points to steady, self-giving love—not how generous you look.

conversation.g: Usually manner of life or citizenship, not small talk.
conversation.s: Ask: “How is my walk?” when you see “conversation.”
conversation.w: On days you feel scattered, remember “conversation” is often your whole walk with God, not your chat skills.

quick.s: Pair “quick” with “dead” in context to see alive vs lifeless.
quick.w: If “the quick and the dead” confuses you, you are in good company: here “quick” means alive—God’s word speaks to living hearts.

peculiar.g: Treasured possession or special people set apart, not “weird.”
peculiar.s: Hear “treasured” when you read peculiar in Titus 2:14.
peculiar.w: When you feel overlooked, the KJV “peculiar” people are treasures set apart—seen by God.

ghost.g: Holy Ghost is the Holy Spirit — older English for the same Person.
ghost.s: Do not read “ghost” as a spooky figure; same Comforter Jesus promised.
ghost.w: If the old word unsettles you, “Holy Ghost” is the same Comforter—the Spirit Jesus promised.

prevent.w: When plans feel stuck, “prevent” in older English often meant “go before” or “meet”—God still goes ahead of you.

suffer.s: When children are named, “suffer” usually means “let them come.”
suffer.w: When you read “suffer the little children,” hear gentle permission: let them come—not only pain language.

virtue.g: Strength, power, or moral excellence going out from Christ — not only modesty.
virtue.s: In Luke 8:46, virtue is power that went out of Him.
virtue.w: When you feel drained, “virtue” in the Gospels can mean power that went out from Christ—His strength, not yours alone.

meat.g: Often solid food (teaching you chew on), not only animal flesh.
meat.s: Contrast milk and meat when growth in doctrine is in view.
meat.w: When teaching feels over your head, “meat” is food you chew on—solid truth for a maturing heart, not a slight.

corn.s: Picture sheaves and harvest, not sweet corn on the cob.
corn.w: When harvest language appears, “corn” is grain in the field—bread and provision—not sweet corn by default.

replenish.g: Fill or populate the earth, not “refill an empty tank” only.
replenish.s: In Genesis 1:28, God fills the earth with people and life.
replenish.w: When life feels empty, replenish in Genesis is about filling and fruitfulness under God’s blessing.

comprehend.g: Sometimes “overcome” or “take hold of,” not only “understand.”
comprehend.s: John 1:5: darkness did not overcome the light.
comprehend.w: When darkness feels winning, John reminds you light is not overcome—truth still stands.

closet.g: Private inner room for prayer, not a clothes closet only.
closet.s: Picture a shut door and secret speech to the Father.
closet.w: When prayer feels exposed, Jesus points to a shut door—quiet honesty with the Father.

bowels.g: Deep affection or compassion — idiom for the seat of feeling.
bowels.s: Read as “tender compassion,” not anatomy lessons.
bowels.w: When compassion feels cold, “bowels” is old idiom for deep tenderness—God-shaped affection, not anatomy.

careful.g: Often “full of care” or anxious, not merely “attentive.”
careful.s: Philippians 4:6 pairs “careful for nothing” with prayer.
careful.w: When worry runs the day, Philippians’ “careful for nothing” is an invitation to carry it to God in prayer.

communicate.g: Often “share” or give materially, not only “talk.”
communicate.s: Hebrews 13:16 ties sharing with doing good.
communicate.w: When you want to bless someone, “communicate” in the epistles often means share materially—love with substance.

flesh.g: Body, human nature, kinship, or weakness — context decides.
flesh.s: Track whether “flesh” means body, self, or unredeemed appetite.
flesh.w: When temptation is loud, “flesh” is not only your body—it can mean self-led desire that needs the Spirit’s lead.

hell.g: Sheol, grave, or Gehenna by context — not one English place every time.
hell.s: Let surrounding verses show whether grave, judgment, or imagery.
hell.w: When the word frightens you, let each verse show whether grave, judgment, or imagery—read with context, not panic.

heart.g: Will, mind, and inner person — not only emotion.
heart.s: “As he thinketh in his heart” is orientation, not only mood.
heart.w: When emotions swing, “heart” in scripture is your inner direction—what you treasure and choose—not only feelings.

soul.g: Life, self, appetite, or person — overlaps with heart and spirit.
soul.s: Ask whether the verse means life, inner life, or appetite.
soul.w: When you feel undone, “soul” often means your life before God—breath, appetite, self—He cares for the whole person.

spirit.g: Breath, attitude, unclean spirit, or Holy Spirit — let the verse choose.
spirit.s: Capitalization in print helps; in audio, context must.
spirit.w: When you are spiritually tired, “spirit” might mean breath, attitude, evil spirit, or Holy Spirit—let the verse decide.

repent.g: Change of mind that shows in turning — not mere regret.
repent.s: Look for fruit that matches the turning.
repent.w: When shame is loud, repentance is turning toward mercy—not wallowing.

justified.g: Declared righteous before God by faith — not “earned by behavior first.”
justified.s: Distinguish standing before God from growth in holiness.
justified.w: When your mind replays failure, justification is God’s righteous verdict on everyone who trusts Christ.

sanctified.g: Set apart for God; status and growth both appear.
sanctified.s: Note past tense “were sanctified” and ongoing “be holy.”
sanctified.w: When growth feels slow, sanctification is both God’s gift and daily becoming more His.

propitiation.g: Wrath absorbed; mercy-seat reality — God’s justice and love meet.
propitiation.s: Think “satisfied justice,” not a cold word only.
propitiation.w: When guilt feels unbearable, this word quietly says God’s justice and love met in Christ—for you.

imputation.g: Counted to your account — Abraham’s faith reckoned as righteousness (idea in Romans 4).
imputation.s: Follow “reckon” and “impute” in Romans 4 in one sitting.
imputation.w: When guilt says “not enough,” imputation is God counting faith to you for righteousness—His gift, not your résumé.

covenant.g: Binding promise God makes and keeps; new covenant in Christ’s blood.
covenant.s: Old and new contrast in Hebrews is about better promises.
covenant.w: When promises feel fragile, covenant is God binding Himself—faithful when we are not.

tabernacle.g: Tent of meeting; God dwelling with a moving people; shadow of Christ.
tabernacle.w: When church feels distant, remember God tabernacled among us—He draws near to sinners in Christ.

atonement.g: Covering of sin; fulfilled in the one final sacrifice.
atonement.s: Hebrews shows one offering versus repeated shadows.
atonement.w: When sin feels sticky, atonement is sin covered and answered—pointing to one final sacrifice.

redemption.g: Bought back — a price paid, ownership changed.
redemption.s: Tie redemption to ransom language without sensationalism.
redemption.w: When life feels owned by fear or habit, redemption is being bought back—belonging to the Lord again.

grace.g: God’s favor you did not earn — not permission to sin.
grace.s: Pair Ephesians 2:8–9 with Romans 6 on new life.
grace.w: On days you feel you have to earn rest, grace is God’s favor meeting you before you proved anything.

faith.g: Trust resting on God’s word; shows in obedience.
faith.s: Faith and works tensions resolve when faith is living.
faith.w: When you cannot see the next step, faith is trust anchored in what God has said.

works.g: Deeds — not ground of salvation, yet faith without deeds is dead.
works.s: Ephesians 2:8–10 holds both grace and workmanship together.
works.w: When you fear you are never doing enough, scripture still says true faith shows up in real love and obedience.

world.g: Age, order, or people on earth — context narrows meaning.
world.s: Ask: moral system, planet, or people?
world.w: When headlines overwhelm, “world” can mean creation, age, or value-system—ask which one the verse targets.

church.g: Assembly — local gathered body and Christ’s people overall.
church.s: Building metaphor is people, not brick idolatry.
church.w: When fellowship hurts, “church” is the called-out assembly—people under Christ’s headship, still being sanctified.

bishop.g: Overseer — pastoral office of care and sound teaching.
bishop.s: Often overlaps elder; watch context for office vs gift.
bishop.w: When leadership disappoints, bishop is overseer language—gifted care, answerable to the Chief Shepherd.

devils.g: Demons, unclean spirits — Christ’s authority is absolute.
devils.s: No fascination — flee to Christ’s word and presence.

wine.g: Fermented drink in many uses; wisdom warns excess.
wine.s: Let context show celebration, medicine, or warning.

winepress.g: Judgment image — treading out God’s wrath in Scripture imagery.
winepress.s: Read as sobering picture, not glee.

temple.g: Building, Christ’s body, or believer — track the referent.
temple.s: Paul’s “your body is the temple” is personal holiness.

let.s: When Paul says “I beseech you… let,” he means “allow this to be so.”
let.w: When you read “let not,” hear permission to stop—God’s commands often free you from what binds.

ensample.g: Pattern or example left for others to follow.
ensample.s: Christ’s steps are the template in 1 Peter 2:21.

eschew.s: Pair with “seek peace” in the same verse.

lust.g: Strong desire — not only sexual; can be craving generally.
lust.s: Name the desire and bring it to God honestly.
lust.w: When desire misleads you, lust is craving that pulls away from God’s good—naming it is the first step toward freedom.

study.g: Be diligent, strive rightly — not only “academic homework.”
study.s: 2 Timothy 2:15 is a workman approved, not proud.
study.w: When the mind races, study is earnest care—to approve what is excellent, not anxious grinding.

strange.g: Foreign, alien, or unusual — context decides.
strange.s: “Strange trial” is unfamiliar testing, not oddness.
strange.w: When you feel like an outsider, strange can mean foreign fire or other gods—keep worship pure and near to God.

superstitious.g: In Acts 17, “very religious” — devout, not “irrational” only.
superstitious.s: Paul bridges from their altar to the unknown God.

list.g: To choose, desire, or please — archaic verb.

firmament.g: Expanse or arch — heavens spread out, not modern “firm plate” debates.
firmament.s: Read poetry as majesty, not modern science footnotes in the margin.

wist.s: Swap in “knew” when it sounds wooden.

wot.g: Know — “we wot that” means “we know that.”

verily.s: When Jesus doubles “Verily, verily,” slow down and listen.

anon.s: Rhymes with “upon” in rhythm — sense is “right away.”

straightway.g: Immediately — same idea as “forthwith” in places.
straightway.s: Narrative speed: obey without dragging feet.

by and by.g: Immediately or soon — not “eventually” in several texts.
by and by.s: Check context: sometimes “at once,” sometimes “later” in older English — compare translations carefully.

carriage.g: Behavior or baggage — context decides (conduct vs what is carried).
carriage.s: In narrative, “carriage” can mean baggage train; in epistles, sometimes “walk.”

curious.g: Skilled, intricate, or prying — context picks.
curious.s: Craftsmanship vs forbidden arts — watch the verse.

meddle.g: Busy oneself in what is not yours — warn trouble.

perfect.g: Complete, mature, finished — not flawless in every modern sense.
perfect.s: Hebrews maturity vs milk is a growth picture.
perfect.w: When you fear you will never measure up, “perfect” often means complete or mature—not impossible personal polish.

comfortable.g: Comforting words or strength — adjective of comfort.
comfortable.w: When you need a steady word, “comfortable” in older English ties to strengthening speech—God speaking courage.

mortify.g: Put to death — kill sin by the Spirit’s help.
mortify.w: When sin feels entrenched, mortify means putting deeds to death by the Spirit—kindness, not self-destruction.

simplicity.w: When you second-guess every motive, simplicity is sincere single-mindedness before God.

shamefacedness.g: Modesty and reverence — especially in 1 Timothy 2.
shamefacedness.w: When culture shouts exposure, shamefacedness is modest reverence—honor, not fear of being seen.

damnation.g: Condemnation or judgment — legal outcome, not a curse word.
damnation.s: Serious, not slang — let the text define which judgment.
damnation.w: When the word sounds harsh, it is serious judgment language in court terms—let scripture define the verdict in view.

press.g: Crowd pressing in — throng around Jesus.
press.w: When crowds surround Jesus in the text, press is a throng drawing near—physical nearness, hunger for Him.

multiply.g: Increase, grow many — people, blessing, or trouble by context.
multiply.s: Ask whether growth is godly or grievous.
multiply.w: When life feels thin or loud, multiply tracks blessing or burden by context—ask which way the verse bends.

reins.g: Kidneys — Hebrew idiom for inner affections; KJV uses “reins.”
reins.s: Read as “deepest motives,” not biology quiz.
reins.w: When desire is hard to name, reins picture inner motives—God tries the heart, not only the face.

science.g: Knowledge — “science falsely so called” is empty knowledge.
science.s: Not modern lab science by default — compare “knowledge.”
science.w: When “science” appears in KJV, it often means knowledge claimed—compare with God’s truth, not modern labs only.

vain.g: Empty, worthless, or idols — “in vain” is emptiness.
vain.w: When efforts feel pointless, vain can mean empty or idol—ask what you are trusting besides the Lord.

subtil.g: Crafty or shrewd — serpent in Eden, not a compliment.
subtil.s: Moral shade: discern good subtlety vs deception.
subtil.w: When someone seems too smooth, subtil is crafty—watch serpent language and choose plain truth.

authority.g: Power, right to command, or sphere — rulers, parents, Christ.
authority.s: All human authority is under God’s.
authority.w: When power scares you, authority in Scripture is ordered—Jesus has final say; earthly power is bounded.

blood.g: Life, sacrifice, covenant — context shows meaning.
blood.s: Trace blood from altar to Christ once for all.
blood.w: When conscience accuses, blood in scripture points to life laid down—atonement that speaks better than sacrifice.

cross.g: Shameful death and glory — offense and power.
cross.s: Boast only in the Lord’s finished work.
cross.w: When self is loud, the cross is shame turned to glory—where boasting dies and mercy rises.

gospel.g: Good news of Christ’s kingdom, death, and resurrection.
gospel.s: Keep the core facts central when “gospel” is used broadly.
gospel.w: When truth feels thin, the gospel is the good news of Christ’s finished work—keep the core facts central.

holiness.g: Set-apartness unto God — moral and positional.
holiness.w: When you feel too ordinary for God, holiness is set-apartness—His gift and daily becoming more like Him.

mercy.g: Loving-kindness and compassion that is not earned.
mercy.s: Often used when someone has no right to expect help — yet God gives it anyway.
mercy.w: In your hardest battles, mercy reminds you God’s kindness is not based on how well you performed today.

peace.g: Quiet rest and wholeness that the world cannot give.
peace.s: Not the same as calm circumstances — Christ’s gift can hold when life is loud.
peace.w: Even when your body hurts or your mind won’t rest, God’s peace can still rule in your heart.

strength.g: Power that shows up most clearly when we are weak.
strength.s: Paul’s testimony: when I am weak, then am I strong — Christ’s strength, not swagger.
strength.w: This is the same strength Paul wrote about — made perfect in weakness.

hope.g: Confident expectation anchored in God, not wishfulness.
hope.s: Hope is sure because the Promiser is faithful.
hope.w: When the future feels blank, biblical hope is steady expectation—because God keeps His word.

fear.g: Reverence or terror — context shows holy fear vs panic.
fear.s: “Fear not” calms panic; “fear God” awakens reverence.
fear.w: When anxiety shouts and worship feels distant, the same Bible pairs “fear not” with holy reverence for God.

joy.g: Deep gladness rooted in God — not hype.
joy.s: Joy can coexist with grief when hope holds.
joy.w: When happiness is gone, joy can still quietly root in Christ—even while you are sad.

longsuffering.g: Patience, slow anger — fruit of the Spirit.
longsuffering.s: God’s longsuffering is room to repent.
longsuffering.w: When patience runs out, longsuffering is Spirit-given room—God patient with us first.

meek.g: Strength under God’s hand — not weakness.
meek.w: When you feel pressed to fight every battle, meekness is strength steadied under God’s hand.

condemnation.g: Judgment — guilty verdict; contrast “no condemnation” in Christ.
condemnation.s: Romans 8:1 is the anchor verse for assurance.
condemnation.w: When accusation rings in your head, “no condemnation” in Christ is the door back to peace.

election.g: God’s choosing — comfort and humility, not arrogance.
election.s: Hold election with calling and holiness.
election.w: When you feel unchosen, election is God’s sure purpose—held with humility and holy living, not pride.

predestination.g: Foreordained purpose — unto conformity to Christ.
predestination.s: Goal is Christlikeness, not fatalistic gloom.
predestination.w: When the future scares you, predestination in Romans is unto Christlikeness—His purpose, your comfort.

adoption.g: Placed as sons — privilege and Spirit witness.
adoption.w: When “orphan” feels true, adoption is sonship by God’s act—Spirit witness, not paperwork.

intercession.g: Praying for another — Christ and the Spirit.
intercession.w: When words fail in prayer, the Spirit and the Son still speak for you—ongoing mercy.

temptation.g: Trial or enticement — James distinguishes sources.
temptation.s: God does not tempt to evil; He provides escape.
temptation.w: When you feel singled out in trial, God does not tempt to evil—He gives escape and faithful company.

resurrection.g: Standing again — Christ first, then His own.
resurrection.s: Hope is embodied — empty tomb matters.
resurrection.w: When death or loss shadows you, resurrection is God’s pledge—Christ’s victory is the church’s hope.

everlasting.g: Age-enduring, eternal — God’s life and punishment both serious.
everlasting.s: Let context show gift of life or severity of judgment.
everlasting.w: When time feels cruel, everlasting life is quality and duration in God—not a rushed slogan.

hell fire.s: Read warnings with trembling mercy — flee to Christ.

new birth.g: Born again — Spirit’s work, not mere decision talk.
new birth.s: Nicodemus needed Spirit, not only argument.

baptism.g: Immersion picture — union with Christ’s death and resurrection.
baptism.s: Distinguish sign from saving work — faith in Christ saves.
baptism.w: When identity feels shaky, baptism is union pictured in water—Christ’s, not human prestige.

communion.g: Fellowship — often Lord’s supper sense in older usage.
communion.s: 1 Corinthians 10 ties cup and bread to one body.
communion.w: When you feel alone at the table, communion is fellowship—shared life in Christ with His people.

offence.g: Stumbling block — trap or cause to fall.
offence.s: Love limits liberty when others stumble.
offence.w: When truth offends, “offence” can mean stumbling block—sometimes the issue is hardness, sometimes love warns.

alms.g: Merciful giving to the poor — not a performance.
alms.s: Pair secret giving (Matthew 6) with a generous heart.
alms.w: When you want to help quietly, alms is mercy shown in giving—without needing applause.

amen.g: “So be it” — firm agreement and truth.
amen.s: When Scripture stacks “amen,” treat it as sealed.
amen.w: When words run out, amen is “so be it”—agreement and trust sealed in prayer.

apostle.g: Sent one — eyewitness ambassadors of Christ with authority.
apostle.s: Distinguish the Twelve/foundation from every “sent” task today.
apostle.w: When leadership disappoints, apostle means sent one—authority tied to Christ’s mission, not ego.

array.g: Dress, equip, or set in order — not only “arrange data.”
array.s: In poetry, array is clothing and dignity.

begat.g: Fathered, brought forth — genealogy and incarnation language.
begat.s: In Matthew 1, trace promise and fulfillment.

begotten.g: Uniquely brought forth — “only begotten” points to the Son.
begotten.s: Hold uniqueness without drifting into confusion about the eternal Son.

beguiled.g: Deceived, led astray — Eve and false teachers.
beguiled.s: Name the lie; return to plain Scripture.

bewitched.g: Deceived or fascinated — not stage magic.
bewitched.s: Paul’s point is gospel clarity stolen by confusion.

bewray.s: Context shows whether betrayal or simple disclosure.

bill.g: Written certificate — often divorce writing in controversy texts.
bill.s: Jesus raises the heart, not paperwork tricks.

blasphemy.g: Speech that dishonors God or claims what is His alone.
blasphemy.s: Distinguish rash words from the unforgivable hardness Jesus warns of.

blemish.g: Spot or defect — purity for sacrifice and character.

blot out.g: Erase debt, remove from record — God’s forgiveness language.
blot out.s: Contrast with names kept in the book of life.

brasen.g: Brass or bronze — altar, serpent, sea (symbolic hardware).
brasen.s: Read as appointed instruments, not lucky charms.

brazen.g: Often brass/bronze — brazen altar, brazen serpent.
brazen.s: The lifted serpent points to Christ — faith, not superstition.

breath.g: Life-breath from God; also Spirit imagery.
breath.s: Every breath is borrowed — live gratefully.
breath.w: When you feel fragile, breath ties life to God’s gift—spirit and body held in His hand.

bridegroom.g: Husband-to-be — Christ and the church imagery.
bridegroom.s: Joy and fidelity — not sentimental fluff.

bruise.g: Crush or wound — Genesis 3:15 and the suffering Servant.
bruise.s: Trace hope from the first promise to the cross.

buckler.s: Pair with “shield” language in the same psalms.

burden.g: Load, oracle, or heavy message — context picks.
burden.s: “Burden” can mean prophetic word, not only weight.

burthen.g: Older spelling of burden — same range of meaning.

bushel.g: Measure — hide or reveal light imagery.
bushel.s: Let good works shine for God’s glory, not vanity.

candlestick.g: Lampstand — tabernacle and “light of the world” imagery.
candlestick.s: Churches as lampstands is responsibility, not décor.

carcase.g: Dead body — ceremonial laws and sober pictures.
carcase.s: Use reverence when reading death texts.

carnal.g: Fleshly, unspiritual — oriented by fallen appetite.
carnal.s: Not “body is bad,” but “self-run life” vs Spirit-led.

cast lots.g: Providence over chance — used for decisions in narrative.

chaste.g: Pure in body and mind — modest love.
chaste.s: Chastity is wholeness, not shame of being human.

chasten.s: Receive discipline as love, not rejection.
chasten.w: When discipline stings, chastening is a Father’s training—love that corrects, not abandons.

chastise.g: Correct sharply when needed — still purposeful.
chastise.s: Distinguish human abuse from God’s righteous rule.

cherubims.g: Cherubim — heavenly guardians and throne imagery.

cleave.g: Cling fast or split apart — opposite meanings by context.
cleave.s: Marriage cleaving vs cursed cleaving — watch the verse.

clothed.g: Put on — often moral or gospel clothing imagery.
clothed.s: “Put on Christ” is daily dressing by faith.

comely.s: Modesty can still be comely — dignity without show.

commend.s: Paul commends people to God’s grace — a tender charge.

communed.s: “Commune with your own heart” is honest self-talk before God.

concision.g: Mutilation — Paul’s sharp word for fleshly confidence.
concision.s: Contrast true circumcision of heart by the Spirit.

conscience.g: Inner witness — trained by truth, not mere feelings.
conscience.s: A seared conscience is dangerous — feed it Scripture.
conscience.w: When guilt whispers, conscience can be clean or seared—bring it to Christ and His word for a true witness.

convert.g: Turn back, restore — soul and direction.
convert.s: Conversion is Godward turn, not a mood.
convert.w: When you feel stuck, convert is turn—God meets the turned heart with forgiveness and new direction.

couch.g: Lie down, rest — sheep and sleep imagery.
couch.s: Picture calm when the Lord makes His people lie down.

creeping.g: Crawling things — creation categories and purity laws.
creeping.s: Order in creation; humility before the Creator.

cruel.s: Cruel masters contrast the gentle yoke of Christ.

crucify.g: Nail to a cross — old man, flesh, and Christ’s death.
crucify.s: Union with Christ’s death is real, not metaphor only.

cup.g: Cup of blessing or wrath — what you drink with God.
cup.s: Jesus drank the bitter cup for us.

curseth.g: Calls down curse — solemn, not slang.
curseth.s: Bless those who curse you — Romans 12.

custom.g: Habit, tax, or ordinary practice — context decides.
custom.s: “After the custom” is routine — not necessarily holy.

cut off.g: Removed from covenant people or life — serious.
cut off.s: Let the weight point you to Christ’s sufficient sacrifice.

defiled.s: Wash in confession and truth — 1 John 1:9.

deliver.g: Rescue, hand over, or birth — track the sense.
deliver.s: Deliver us from evil is daily dependence.
deliver.w: When trouble presses, deliver is rescue language—God as the One who draws you out, again and again.

deliverance.g: Rescue realized — God’s help in trouble.
deliverance.s: Remember past deliverances when new fears rise.

deny.g: Disown, refuse — Jesus warns and encourages.

depart.g: Go away, remove, or die — gentle or solemn.
depart.s: “Depart from me” is sober when Jesus says it.

despise.g: Treat as nothing — God, wisdom, or neighbor.
despise.s: Do not despise small beginnings of grace.

devour.g: Consume — Satan as roaring lion; strife devours.
devour.s: Stay sober; resist him steadfast in faith.

diligence.s: Diligence is quiet faithfulness, not panic.
diligence.w: When you want to quit, diligence is steady care—faithful next steps without theatrics.

dissimulation.g: Hypocrisy — hiding what you truly are.
dissimulation.s: Love without dissimulation is sincere brotherly love.

doctrine.g: Teaching — sound words to build and guard.
doctrine.s: Test all teaching by Christ and the apostles.
doctrine.w: When opinions fly, doctrine is teaching to be held—tested by Scripture, lived with humility.

draught.g: Catch of fish; also drain — context picks.
draught.s: Miraculous draughts show who rules sea and heart.

dross.g: Waste slag from metal — impurity to purge.
dross.s: Refining imagery: God purges, not to destroy you.

drunken.s: Be filled with the Spirit instead — Ephesians 5.

dumb.s: Healing stories restore voice — picture gospel opening mouths.

durst.s: Swap “dared” mentally when you hit durst.

edify.g: Build up — church speech and love.
edify.s: Ask: does this word build or tear down?

elder.g: Older man; also office of oversight — context.
elder.s: Respect and honor where Scripture commands.

embrace.s: Ecclesiastes pairs embrace with refraining — seasons.

end.g: Goal, outcome, or final stop — teleology matters.
end.s: “The end of your faith” is salvation of souls.

engender.s: Trace sin’s birth to death; grace’s birth to life.

envious.g: Jealous of another’s good — rots bones.
envious.s: Rejoice with those who rejoice — kill envy.

epistle.s: These letters are God-breathed rule for faith.

err.g: Wander off course — morally and intellectually.
err.s: Gentle restoration for the erring — James 5.

espoused.s: Paul’s bridal language is devotion, not drama.

esteem.g: Value, regard, or reckon — context picks.
esteem.s: Esteem others better — humility in community.

eyeservice.g: Service only when watched — hollow obedience.
eyeservice.s: Serve as unto the Lord — heart, not performance.

faint.g: Grow weak, lose heart — God strengthens.
faint.s: Do not faint in well doing — season of reaping comes.

familiar spirit.s: Seek the Lord, not the dead — sober warning.

fast.s: Fasting pairs with feasting on God’s word.

fat.g: Rich, best portion — offerings and abundance.
fat.s: “Fatness” can mean deep satisfaction in God.

fatlings.g: Young fat cattle — feast and sacrifice imagery.
fatlings.s: Parables use feast language — come to the banquet.

fearfully.g: Wonderfully — awe, not terror, in Psalm 139.
fearfully.s: You are fearfully set apart — dignity from the Maker.

fiends.g: Fierce companions or mockers — rare word.
fiends.s: Job’s loneliness language — read with compassion.

filthy.s: Christ clothes the filthy with righteousness.

firstborn.s: Christ is firstborn among many brethren.

firstfruits.g: First part of harvest — pledge of full crop.
firstfruits.s: Resurrection is firstfruits — more glory coming.

flattery.g: Smooth words that mislead — guard the naive.

fleshly.g: According to the flesh — unspiritual mindset.
fleshly.s: Not “body bad,” but “self on the throne.”

fowls.g: Birds — care of God and parable seed.
fowls.s: If God feeds fowls, He will sustain you.

frankincense.g: Incense offering — prayer and worship aroma.
frankincense.s: Picture tabernacle worship — Christ is better.

freewill.s: God loves a cheerful giver — 2 Corinthians 9.

gainsay.s: Christ’s witnesses speak boldly when opposed.

gender.s: James: lust conceives and sins when full grown.

gentiles.g: Nations — non-Jewish peoples; grace to the world.
gentiles.s: One new man — Jew and Gentile in Christ.

gird.s: “Gird up the loins of your mind” is alert holiness.

girdle.g: Belt — priestly dress and John the Baptist.
girdle.s: Symbol of strength and office — read visually.

glean.g: Gather leftovers — mercy for the poor.
glean.s: Boaz’s field is a picture of generous provision.

glede.g: Bird of prey — eagle-like in prophecy.
glede.s: Rare word — read as swift destroying bird in judgment poetry.

harlot.g: Prostitute — literal and covenant unfaithfulness imagery.
harlot.s: Spiritual adultery is chasing lovers that cannot save.

haste.s: Wait on the Lord beats proud haste.

haughty.g: Lifted up in pride — God resists.
haughty.s: Humble yourself under God’s hand — 1 Peter 5:6.

hearken.s: Hearkening is more than ears — it is doing.

heaviness.g: Grief, depression of spirit — God meets it.
heaviness.s: Oil of joy for heaviness — Isaiah 61.
